content.thinking:
I'm noticing the flag rollout was gradual, starting around 17:42 with a partial percentage (63/200) and reaching full rollout by 17:43, yet the logged change event timestamp of 17:47:37 comes after errors began—likely just marking when the toggle was formally committed rather than when it actually took effect.

This confirms the ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py is directly tied to the monthly-spend-feature flag being toggled on, with no accompanying code deployment or config change. I'm confident this fits the feature-flag-toggle failure mode.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was rolled from off to on, and the on-path in spend_summary.py divides by zero (some shoppers apparently have a zero divisor, e.g. zero purchase count) causing account-page requests to fail. Error rate on io-shop's account page climbs in lockstep with the flag's rollout percentage (63/200 evaluations at 17:42 turning on, then 100% on from 17:43 onward), matching the ZeroDivisionError bursts and the metrics onset at 17:42.

supporting_evidence.claim: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47

hypotheses.summary: If the flag toggle is judged not to be the cause, no deployment or dependency issue was found in the change/log windows examined; the only recorded change in this window is the flag toggle itself, so absent that this incident's cause is undetermined.
